description: Rerail checks the code a coding agent writes against the repository's rules, on the developer's machine, and steers the agent to fix what breaks them. It hooks into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OMP and Pi, and ships rule packs, most ported from common linters.
rules: Install with `npx @neralabs/rerail setup` in the repository. A coding agent runs `npx @neralabs/rerail setup --relay` and asks the person each question it prints, as written.
Rerail is off in a repository until it is started there: `/rerail-start`, or `rerail start` in a terminal.
Codex invokes Rerail commands as `$rerail-…`; every other coding agent as `/rerail-…`. `/rerail` lists them all.

Rules belong to one repository. Create one with `/rerail-create`: test the draft with `rerail rules test <draft.json>`, then `rerail rules add <draft.json>`; a rule the person asked for is added only after they confirm the read-back.
To change only where a rule applies, a Rerail pack's JSON rule included, `rerail rules show <id>` prints it as a draft: change its `scope` alone and test it with `rerail rules test <draft.json>`.

After the person confirms a draft `rerail rules show <id>` printed, run `rerail rules add <draft.json>`; the person approves it in the dashboard. A pack rule, or an edit of an approved rule, is saved as a copy that turns the original off once approved.

A pack's rule written in `.rerail`, such as the Django pack's, cannot be copied yet, so its scope cannot be changed: `rerail rules show <id>` prints its file, and the person turns it on or off, or changes its mode, in the dashboard.
A rule's mode is `log` (recorded only) or `steer` (its guidance is sent to the agent).

Write a code rule as a JSON draft whose `rule` is a `rerail.policy/v1` document; `rerail rules add` takes only JSON. A rule pack may ship rules written in `.rerail`, which sessions run; `rerail rules test <file>.rerail` runs the file's tests.

When Rerail reports violations of your last edit, fix them, or tell the user in one line why you won't and record that line with `rerail feedback <rule-id> '<that line>'`. On Windows, or for a line with `'`, give `-` in its place and the line on stdin.
Rule packs are npm packages named `@neralabs/rerail-pack-<id>`; manage them with `rerail packs list`, `add`, `remove`, `update` and `recommend`.

Update with `rerail update` (`/rerail-update`, `$rerail-update` in Codex): it updates core, then each rule pack to the newest version that fits. After an update from 0.1.5 or earlier, run `rerail packs update` once.

Packs that port a linter are linter-equivalent to it, and set-up turns their rules on and off to match the repository's own linter config; after that config changes, `rerail packs calibrate` reads it again.

A rule pack's `pack.json` may give a rule `dimensions`: `risk`, `layer` and `severity` together, from the fixed values in docs/rule-dimensions.md, and an optional `hazard` id. Cores before 0.2.2 refuse the field. Side packs are a design, not built.

A rule for one worktree only is a rule document in that worktree's `.rerail/rules/<name>.json`: it runs there and in no other checkout, needs no install or add, and `rerail packs list` run there shows whether it loaded.

When Rerail seems not to record or steer, `rerail status` says whether the daemon runs and what to do; `rerail daemon stop`, then `rerail daemon start`, restarts it. `/rerail-bug-report` helps fix the person's own rule or report a Rerail bug.

The features in docs/internal-testing.md, `rerail scan`, conversation rules and `block` mode among them, are unsupported and off until their `RERAIL_EXPERIMENTAL_<FEATURE>` variable is set. Suggest one only when the person asks for it.
